transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Summit Partnerships), Elena Garcia (Summit CTO), Marcus Lee (Summit Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate you squeezing this in. i'm maya from redwood, account owner for this region. 
[00:12] Raj: no problem, maya. thanks. excited to learn more about what you all are building. quick intro — i'm raj, i run partnerships at summit. we build GPU clusters and also run a managed private cloud for inference customers.
[00:25] Elena: hi, elena here, cto. we primarily sell racks and managed infra to mid-enterprise ai teams, and exploring tighter infra partnerships for inference platforms.
[00:36] Liam: hi team, liam, solutions engineer at redwood. i'll dive into technical bits and benchmark approach.
[00:42] Marcus: marcus, eng manager. we'll be the day-to-day folks if we move forward.
[00:47] Maya: awesome. agenda — quick intros and goals, high-level integration models, technical constraints (network, kms, compliance), performance/benchmarking approach, and go-to-market/commercial stuff, then next steps. sound good?
[00:58] Raj: yep, good.
[01:05] Maya: quick question — what's your initial interest? is this partnership for channel/resell, or deeper systems integration like offering redwood private as an add-on to your managed infra?
[01:17] Raj: both, potentially. we see customers asking for a managed inference platform with low-latency support. some want a hosted api, others want on-prem or vpc-connected offerings. we'd like to evaluate a few partners to white-label or co-manage.
[01:33] Elena: key constraints: we need strong KMS integration, proof of encryption-at-rest and in-transit, and SOC2-like audit trails. also some clients require air-gapped on-prem installs.
[01:46] Liam: sounds familiar. redwood supports hosted api, dedicated pools, and private (vpc/on-prem). our private deployment can be customer-controlled with a local control plane; we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM vendors for on-prem. 
[02:05] Marcus: do you support bringing-your-own-images or only prebuilt runtime? some customers want to run specific operator stacks.
[02:15] Liam: we support a few runtime variants; for private deployments we can run customer-provided images under an approved security review. there is a vetting step though.
[02:27] Raj: how does networking look for vpc mode? do you do peering, transit gateway, or agent-based egress?
[02:35] Liam: multiple options. we can do VPC peering or private link style connections. for on-prem we have a secure tunnel back to the control plane, or customers can run the full control plane locally (air-gapped). some customers prefer direct peering to avoid public endpoints.
[02:53] Elena: what's your model for KV caching and batching? we worry about latency with larger batches if we co-locate.
[03:03] Liam: our serving runtime has smart KV cache to reuse prefix state; batching is tunable. you can configure latency SLOs vs throughput via batch windows and reserved capacity. in dedicated pools you get predictable qps. small caveat: for some quantized models you need specific kernel support on the GPU, so the exact latency depends on model variant and sequence length.
[03:26] Marcus: got it. and what about model variants — folks sometimes want to offer smaller / quantized versions as fallback to save cost.
[03:33] Maya: yep, we support model routing policies — e.g., route to cheaper quantized variant if higher latency is acceptable, or fallback to hosted if private pool is saturated.
[03:44] Raj: bandwidth & egress pricing is often a dealbreaker. we run across customers worried about token-level ingress/egress costs. how are costs typically structured?
[03:54] Maya: hosted is per-token; dedicated is reserved capacity commit with a monthly fee, and private deployments are a platform license plus infra costs. for partner channel deals we can explore revenue-share or discounted reserved capacity for white-label bundles.
[04:10] Elena: security — do you have audit logs at the request level? we need to map to our SIEM.
[04:17] Liam: yes, request-level audit logs, plus role-based access controls and SAML SSO. logs can be shipped to your splunk/datadog or GCS/azure storage.
[04:27] Raj: great. could you share SOC2 and architecture diagrams?
[04:30] Maya: absolutely — i'll send those after the call.
[04:34] [05:00] (brief crosstalk, someone dropping audio)
[05:20] Marcus: speaking of diagrams, latency budgets are critical. can you get sample p95 numbers for common models on your dedicated infra vs private deployment on our hardware?
[05:32] Liam: we can — plan would be: 1) redwood sends a benchmark plan with model list, sequence lengths, and measurement metrics; 2) summit provisions a test pool or shares access; 3) we run benchmarks and share p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.
[05:49] Raj: do you do remote benchmarking or do you prefer on-site? some customers don't want remote access to their cluster.
[05:57] Liam: we can do both. remote via a temporary test user or run our bench harness locally if you share results. for on-prem air-gapped we can provide a runner to be executed in your environment.
[06:12] Elena: any restrictions on GPU vendors/drivers? some of our racks use mixed nvidia amd blades.
[06:21] Liam: we primarily optimize for nvidia drivers (A100/H100) and some upcoming Mx-like variants; AMD support is more limited and depends on the runtime kernels. we can map compatibility table in the doc.
[06:36] Raj: we heard you recently added quantization-friendly paths and kernel selection. how mature are those?
[06:44] Liam: fairly mature for Llama-family and some other open models; we do kernel selection based on model arch and target hardware. small models and 4-bit quantization are well tested; larger model families still in progress but supported in many cases.
[06:58] Marcus: for an initial pilot, we want 99ms p95 for a 4k length? is that realistic?
[07:06] Liam: 4k is tricky — p95 depends on model and GPU. for smaller models at 4k it might be achievable on H100 with correct kernels and batching, but we need to test. we'll call this a benchmark action item.
[07:19] [07:40] Raj: commercial — if we bundle redwood as part of our managed offering, what does partner pricing look like? referral fee vs co-sell?
[07:50] Maya: there's flexibility; we often do a referral credit + discounted reserved capacity for partners who bring customers. for co-sell we negotiate margins and go-to-market joint templates. we can share sample partner agreement language.
[08:05] Raj: nice. do you have marketplace listings? customers sometimes prefer to buy from cloud marketplaces.
[08:11] Maya: yes, we have marketplace listings on major clouds and are expanding. private deployments are licensed directly.
[08:18] Elena: about support — what SLA tiers do you offer for private customers vs dedicated?
[08:25] Liam: dedicated customers get SLA-backed latency+uptime tiers; private customers on enterprise licensing get priority support and optional managed services. for pilot we usually do 24x7 support window for production pilots.
[08:39] Marcus: runbook integration — can the redwood console push metrics into our observability stack?
[08:46] Liam: yes, we export metrics/traces and per-route token-level costs. there's also webhook hooks and tracing headers you can map into your existing dashboards.
[08:57] Raj: ok good. anything we should be aware of regarding compliance for our european customers? data residency?
[09:04] Maya: we have regioned control planes and data residency options; private deployments allow keeping data inside customer networks. for hosted we offer EU regions.
[09:12] Elena: for some regulated customers, we need full auditability plus offline install. how heavy is the offline on-prem install?
[09:20] Liam: it's a full control plane bundle; it's heavier but doable. we'd run a joint security review. typically that takes a few weeks for the checklist and then deployment depending on customer ops capacity.
[09:34] [10:00] (brief pause)
[10:15] Raj: curious — any reference partners doing this today? examples of a hardware partner + redwood bundle?
[10:24] Maya: yes, we have a few partners — i can share anonymized case studies. petacompute and aurora-systems have done private deployments and co-sell motions. i'll attach notes.
[10:35] Elena: perfect. one final tech question — how do you ensure isolation of model weights and keys if we host customer workloads on shared infra?
[10:44] Liam: we provide tenant isolation layers, encrypted model stores, and customer-specific keys. for strict isolation we recommend dedicated pools or on-prem private installs.
[10:56] Marcus: sounds good.
[11:05] Maya: ok to recap — we'll: send partner deck + SOC2 and architecture diagrams; liam will draft a benchmark plan; schedule a deep-dive with your infra team next week; raj will share suggested commercial models and internal partner approval steps.
[11:22] Raj: yes that's good.
[11:26] Elena: timeline wise we'd like to kick a pilot jan 10-20 window if approvals go well.
[11:33] Maya: noted, we'll aim to have docs and plan out by 12/30 so you can review before the new year.
[11:40] [12:00] (small filler chatter)
[12:20] Marcus: quick note — we'll include our network diagrams in the dropbox link and give a read-only account for bench users.
[12:31] Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and the deep-dive. 
[12:40] Raj: thanks all.
[12:44] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[12:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors for technical terms (eg \"KV cash\" instead of KV cache, some proper names garbled). Speakers sometimes labeled generically in the raw export; cleaned slightly but kept natural speech and filler words.
